headline: Mechanistic models extract regulatory structure from expression measurements
label: Mechanistic Models Of Expression
summary: Recent preprints fit ODE models to zebrafish RNA-seq and yeast imaging data, linking model parameters to developmental and inheritance dynamics.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of explicit model structure to recover regulatory organization from expression or imaging measurements. The zebrafish study fits a semi-mechanistic ODE transcription model to RNA-seq to derive expression clusters tied to the maternal-to-zygotic transition, while PRNODE jointly estimates mother and daughter protein regulatory networks via ODEs with a fused group-lasso, quantifying inheritance across yeast lineages. The state-bridge preprint takes a different route, using the Universal Cell Embedding foundation model to map 22,161 significant bridges among 614 biological states, a data-driven rather than mechanistic approach. velotest adds a statistical check on RNA velocity embeddings, assessing whether trajectory visualizations preserve high-dimensional structure. The newest contribution is the explicit linkage of fitted parameters to inheritance and transition biology, rather than descriptive embeddings alone.
